pathogen.value: Ascaridia galli, a large intestinal roundworm

how_it_spreads.value: birds swallow worm eggs from contaminated feed or water
eggs are very hardy and can survive a long time in the environment
free-range birds are at higher risk because they pick up eggs from the ground, possibly aided by earthworms carrying the eggs

key_symptoms.value: gut blockage and bloody intestinal inflammation in heavy infections
general unthriftiness, drooping wings and a pale head
emaciation and stunted growth, mainly in birds under 12 weeks old
worms occasionally seen in droppings or even inside laid eggs

diagnosis.value: found by seeing worms or their eggs in droppings, or occasionally worms inside eggs

treatment_overview.value: treated with deworming medication given in feed, water, or as a single dose; effectiveness varies by drug and by the bird's age

summary.value: Ascaridia galli is a large roundworm that lives in the small intestine of chickens and turkeys and is picked up by swallowing hardy worm eggs from contaminated ground, feed or water. Heavy infections cause poor growth, fewer eggs, intestinal damage and can be fatal, but they are treatable with deworming medication.
